notes: Takes the broken plural ثِقَال (thiqāl). Opposite: خَفِيف (khafīf, 'light').
To call a person dull or unpleasant, Arabic uses the set phrase ثَقِيلُ الظِّلِّ (thaqīlu ẓ-ẓill, literally 'heavy of shadow') or ثَقِيلُ الدَّمِ ('heavy of blood').

senses.definition: Of great physical weight; hard to lift or move.

examples.emotion: exasperated, feeling the physical strain of carrying a large bag

senses.definition: Hard to bear or endure; oppressive, intense, or tiresome.

notes: While 'thāqīl' literally means heavy, it is often used metaphorically to describe someone who is difficult to deal with, boring, or tiresome.

senses.definition: Having a great weight; not light.

examples.emotion: exasperated, feeling the physical strain of carrying a large bag

senses.definition: Difficult to handle or cope with; tedious.

examples.emotion: annoyed and impatient, describing someone who drains your energy

faults.why: Wrong transliteration 'thāqīl' (has a short 'a': thaqīl) and misses the idiom ثَقِيلُ الظِّلِّ.
